name: PT. Polychem Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Polychem Indonesia — the cash is the value, and the spread does not earn its depreciation
frontmatter.summary: Polychem runs one Merak site after closing polyester: a glycol train at a fifth of nameplate, an ethoxylate train at nine tenths. The third quarter of 2026 was a gross loss and the last year's economics do not cover depreciation, so the going concern is worth about nothing. The equity is the net cash and the land option, and the price is already about one and a half times the net liquid assets. SELL, target Rp108 against Rp192.
thesis: The operating business does not earn its depreciation: gross margin of 1.6% in FY2026E against SG&A of 2.5% of revenue leaves EBIT of US$-1.9m, below the US$4.1m depreciation charge, and the DCF therefore pays US$-9.7m for two trains and a site [S4, S5].

The reported profit is not operating: nine months of 2026 net profit of US$4.4m sits on gross profit of US$3.8m, with US$2.6m of other gains and a US$1.3m fair-value gain on the listed portfolio closing the gap [S4].

The balance sheet is the value: cash of US$20.9m and no bank debt plus a separate US$8.9m listed portfolio, against a market capitalisation of IDR746.7bn [S4, S0]. The price is above the liquid assets, not below them, so what the buyer pays for today is the land option and a spread recovery.

The land is a real option and we no longer put a probability on it: 853,205 square metres under building rights at Merak, Cilegon and Karawang, carried at US$65.1m cost and never depreciated [S5, F30, F31]. A sale would realise roughly book value less the operating EV given up, but no filing states a buyer, a price or a timetable, so the base case does not pay for it.
The stock is a decision on the glycol train and the site, not a spread trade: a shutdown, a conversion or a sale of the site would move the value more than the ethoxylate margin [S2, S10].

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results and the board's decision on the ethylene glycol train
Government decision on the industry association's safeguard and anti-dumping requests for olefins, aromatics and plastics
First-quarter 2027 financial statements, the first clean read on the post-polyester cost base
Annual general meeting: dividend resolution and auditor reappointment

blocks.text: **SELL, target Rp108 against Rp192, expected return -44.0%.** This revision moves the rating from the published ADD of 7 November 2026 and its target of two hundred and eighteen rupiah. Three things changed in the model, and the bridge from the old call is at the end of this section.

**First, the site bridge is gone.** The previous target carried the land at book value less the operating EV, multiplied by an unsourced quarter. That number was about a third of the base value, it was applied identically in all three scenarios, so the bull never got the site in full and the base got it for free. The company has not announced a sale, a buyer, a price or a timetable, and I cannot register a source that gives a probability. The base case now values the going concern and the cash, and shows the land's carrying value so the reader can size the option; a full-value sale would add a multiple of the gap between the two. **Second, the margin no longer steps up.** FY2026E is built as nine months booked plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate, which produces an effective gross margin of 1.6%. The previous model then jumped to a 1.8% input for FY2027E, a step sourced only to the nine-month average that the losing quarter already dilutes. The forecast now holds the last actual year's economics, which is what the most-likely method requires. **Third, one haircut on the portfolio, not two.** The quoted portfolio used to carry a realisability haircut in the bridge and then the house liquidity discount on the target, about a third in total on the same asset. It is carried at fair value here and the house discount applies once, to the shares [S4, F19].

The variant view is not that the company is bad — it is that the equity is a cash pile with a loss-making converter attached, and that the price already pays for more than the cash. Cash of US$20.9m plus the US$8.9m quoted portfolio is about three quarters of the IDR746.7bn market capitalisation, or roughly a hundred and forty rupiah a share against the Rp192 price. The premium is the land option and a spread recovery that no filing supports; whether the spread ever covers depreciation is the question, and at the last two years' margins it does not. What would change the view is a land sale with terms, a shutdown of the glycol train, or a trade remedy that reaches the ethoxylate slate. None is announced.

**The bridge from the old call.** Removing the land bridge takes about seventy rupiah a share off the base case. Holding the spread at the last actual instead of the stepped-up input takes the largest single slice, about a hundred rupiah. The September net cash adds about fifteen, the single portfolio haircut about nine, and the rest is the cost-of-capital and exchange-rate move. That takes the base case to Rp103; at the scenario weights the bear falls from a positive value to the model floor and the bull to Rp331, giving the weighted Rp135 and, after the 20.0% liquidity discount, Rp108, a -44.0% total return.

PT Polychem Indonesia runs one site at Merak, Banten, after the permanent closure of the polyester division approved in November 2025 [S2, S6]. What is left is an ethylene glycol train of 233,600 t/yr nameplate, run deliberately at low rates, and an ethylene-oxide-derivatives (ethoxylate) train of 80,000 t/yr, run at about nine tenths of capacity and the better-margin product [S2, F5, F6]. Sales are almost all into Java [S4]. One supplier, PT Ecogreen Oleochemicals, provided US$83.6m of the raw materials used in the nine months to September 2026, about three fifths of cost of goods sold [S4, F11, F12]. No single holder controls the company: Provestment Limited holds 49.5%, PT Gajah Tunggal Tbk 25.6% and PT Satya Mulia Gemilang 10.4%, with 14.5% in public hands [S2, F45, F46, F47]. Provestment and Gajah Tunggal are named as stockholders and related parties; Ecogreen is not among the related parties disclosed in the notes and appears only as a supplier above a tenth of purchases [S4].

This is a converter, not a resource business: the spread between a palm-derived feedstock and a sold specification is the entire P&L, and the spread is quoted quarterly. With one segment and one site, there is no mix story. The strategy announced by management is to shift capacity from glycol, which it says still contributes negatively, to ethoxylate, which it says carries better margins [S2].

Indonesian petrochemical utilisation is two thirds of capacity or less on dumped Chinese and Middle Eastern imports, and the industry association is asking the government for safeguards rather than reporting a demand recovery [S7, S10]. Demand grows with GDP and packaging; supply is the problem.

The association's remit matters for the thesis. INAPLAS represents olefins, aromatics and plastics, and the safeguard and anti-dumping requests it has filed cover those product groups [S10]. Polychem's ethoxylate and EOD output — the better-margin line — is a surfactant, not an olefin, aromatic or plastic, and is outside that remit. Any remedy would therefore reach the glycol/MEG chain and the plastics reference price, not the ethoxylate slate: the revenue it could reprice is the glycol line, which management says is loss-making, not the majority of the company's output. I have narrowed the claim accordingly, and the bull case does not assume a remedy lifts both trains.

Moat is weak: the feedstock comes from one supplier, the technology is licensed, and the product is a commodity sold on a formula [S2, S4]. Five forces are all adverse — supplier power in Ecogreen, buyer power in a handful of Java converters and traders, new entry capped only by the dump, substitution from imported surfactants, and rivalry on price. The one external influence that helps is a trade remedy, and it is slow.

**Revenue.** Nine months of 2026 were US$140.8m, annualised on a fourth quarter at the third-quarter rate; the driver was feedstock pass-through, not demand, with raw materials used of US$113.8m against revenue of US$140.8m [S4, F9, F11]. The ethoxylate train is already at nine tenths of capacity, so FY2027E growth of 4.0% is the palm-linked carry-through less the house Brent path, and the later years are at Indonesian chemicals demand growth [S4].

**Margins.** The gross margin is the whole story. Nine months printed about three per cent, the half year a hair under five, and the third quarter a gross loss [S4, F10, F38, F44]. Dollar gross profit for the nine months rose to US$3.8m from US$1.3m in the same period a year earlier, so the deterioration is in the third quarter, not the trend [S4, F10, F43]. The full year therefore lands near 1.6%. I hold that into the forecast: the latest quarter is the most recent and most complete read, and the previous step up to a two-and-a-half per cent input was the one place the model drifted from its own anchor. On this basis EBIT is US$-1.8m against depreciation of US$4.3m — the converter does not cover its own capital consumption.

**Costs and the palm link.** Palm feedstock is three fifths of COGS [S4, F11, F12] and is not a template driver; the template links Brent at 5.0% of COGS with 90.0% pass-through, which is worth about nothing to this P&L. The red team asks whether holding a fixed margin percentage assumes full pass-through of the deck's CPO path while the model states nine tenths. It does assume it, and the 2026 tape is the evidence that the assumption holds for this input: revenue and the raw-material line both rose by about a third, the raw materials slightly faster, and dollar gross profit still rose from US$1.6m to a nine-month US$3.8m. A tenth leak on a cost rise of that size would have taken the spread to zero; it did not. The nine tenths is the Brent link, not the palm link, and the bear case carries a palm leak through a negative spread.

**Cash and the balance sheet.** Two separate assets at 30 September 2026: cash and cash equivalents of US$20.9m and other financial assets of US$8.9m in listed equity securities, with no bank debt and liabilities that are trade payables, accruals and taxes [S4, F19, F26]. Working capital is under one per cent of revenue because the supplier funds the business: payables roughly double receivables [S4]. Capex is a fraction of one per cent of revenue in FY2026E, nine-month actual plus a quarter at the run-rate; the plant is being sweated, and the useful lives disclosed in the annual accounts, five to twenty years for machinery and ten to twenty for buildings, against net PP&E of US$92.8m of which US$65.1m is non-depreciable land, mean the remaining depreciable life is short rather than the two decades the gross figure implies, so replacement cannot be deferred past the end of the decade and capex resets to the depreciation rate from FY2031E [S5, F7, F31, F36].

**Earnings quality.** The 2026 net profit is not operating: other gains, FX and the fair-value gain on the listed portfolio account for the whole of it [S4, F18, F20]. Accruals are not the issue — the balance sheet is cash-rich and payables-funded — but the profit line is. The tax charge is 4.0% because the US$154.2m accumulated loss absorbs almost all of a profit that is mostly interest and gains [S4, F17]; that shield is the main reason a capital return would be tax-efficient, and it is not modelled because no resolution announces one [S9].

**Forecast versus actual.** Nine months of 2026 revenue and gross profit are close to the annualised run-rate in the model; the Q4-at-Q3 construction is the only judgement, and it sits on the conservative side of the nine-month average by design [S4, S3].

DCF is the only method that fits: FY2025A EBITDA is US$0.8m after a US$4.1m depreciation charge, so the EBITDA is little more than the depreciation add-back and EV/EBITDA is a multiple of an accounting entry, while a P/E on a profit made of fair-value gains values the portfolio twice. The weights are DCF at 100%.

Cost of capital is 11.0%: the risk-free rate of 5.0% plus an unlevered beta of 0.90, taken from the industry default, applied to the sum of the mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and the country premium of 2.5%, which gives a cost of equity of 11.0%; with effectively no debt (0.4% of the capital structure) the WACC is 11.0%.

The DCF enterprise value is US$-9.7m. That is not a typo: EBIT is negative in every explicit year, capex normalises to the depreciation rate once the remaining life runs out, and the perpetuity therefore has a negative FCFF. The operating business is worth about nothing as a going concern at the last actual spread; the model does not attempt to value the alternative — shutting the plant and selling or developing the land — because no filing states the terms. Terminal value is 93.6% of the gross PV, which is the signature of a business whose value sits in the option, not the cash flow.

Equity is therefore the September net liquid assets the DCF uses — cash of US$20.9m plus US$8.9m of quoted securities, less lease liabilities — plus the DCF enterprise value of US$-9.7m. That gives Rp93 per share, rolled forward a year at the cost of equity to Rp103. The quoted portfolio is carried at its market value with no separate realisability haircut; the house liquidity discount on the shares is applied once, at the target, and the pre-discount values are shown so the reader can see what it costs.

**The land.** The 853,205 square metres across Merak, Cilegon and Karawang is carried at US$65.1m and never depreciated [S5, F31]. A buyer at book, less the operating EV given up, would produce a bridge item of roughly book minus the DCF EV; the previous version carried a quarter of that in every scenario. I have removed it. The probability was unsourced, it was a third of the base value, and neither the bull nor the base was internally consistent with it. A reader who believes a sale is likely should add that gap to the target; a reader who does not should use the target as printed. The bull case at Rp331 still excludes it, so it is a floor for the sale case, not a ceiling.
**Cross-checks.**

The FCFE yield is 6.3% — a little above the risk-free rate of 5.0%, and it is retained cash rather than a distribution: the group pays no dividend and spends almost nothing on capex, so the cash stays inside the company [S4, S9]. The multiples in the table use the model's forecast net-debt line, which now starts from the 30 September cash of US$20.9m but does not include the US$8.9m quoted portfolio; the DCF's net debt adds it. On the DCF's basis FY2027E EV/EBITDA would be roughly two thirds of the printed 7.0x, and either number is meaningless for a business whose EBITDA is almost entirely its depreciation charge.
The weights are bear 25.0%, base 50.0% and bull 25.0%; they sum to one.

Bear at 25.0%: the third-quarter gross loss becomes the run-rate and then worsens as the palm feedstock keeps rising; the converter earns a negative spread and burns working capital and cash. In that case the equity is worth less than net cash, because the cash is what funds the loss. The printed Rp0 is the engine's floor on a negative equity value, not a valuation: unclipped, the bear DCF is about minus twenty rupiah a share, because the negative perpetuity at that spread takes the operating EV to roughly a sixth more than the net liquid assets. We keep the floor rather than the unclipped number because limited liability is the economic floor and because the alternative — a shutdown that preserves the cash and sells the land — cannot be valued without the realisation we have refused to assume: cash of US$20.9m plus US$8.9m of quoted securities plus land carried at US$65.1m would exceed the base case several times over, which is a statement about the book value of land bought decades ago, not about a bid that exists. The reader can see the floor and the carrying value and judge the option; the target does not pay for it. The sensitivity grid also shows zero operating value at a margin two points lower with growth two points higher, so below break-even the converter consumes the cash rather than throwing it off.
Base at 50.0%: last actual economics hold, the plant runs, no land sale, Rp103.

Bull at 25.0%: a trade remedy lifts the domestic reference price and the ethoxylate spread settles about a point and a half above base, at Rp331. The remedy reaches olefins, aromatics and plastics, not ethoxylates [S10], so this is a reference-price effect on the glycol chain, not a demand recovery.

One caveat: the growth shock in both scenarios is applied to every forecast year including FY2026E, so the bear's FY2026E revenue and the bull's are re-cut even though nine months are banked. The base anchor is unchanged; the scenarios are a sensitivity on the whole path, not a re-forecast of the banked year.

Downside risks, likelihood x impact: an anti-dumping duty that also catches surfactant imports (low x high); the glycol train shut without a land sale (medium x medium); the related-party loan not repaid (medium x low); HGB rights on part of the land expiring from 2027 (low x high, because it removes the option). Upside: a remedy on olefins (medium x high); a land sale with terms (low x very high); a capital return after a deficit reduction (low x medium).

There is no disclosed controlling shareholder: Provestment Limited holds 49.5%, PT Gajah Tunggal Tbk 25.6% and PT Satya Mulia Gemilang 10.4%, so the three holders above five per cent together hold 85.5% and the public 14.5% [S2, F37, F45, F46, F47]. The float is above the exchange floor but thin, and average daily turnover is small enough that the house rule applies a 20.0% liquidity discount to the target — measured ADTV of IDR0.2bn. That is the house rule in the engine, applied to every component including cash; I show the pre-discount value (Rp135 weighted, Rp103 base) so the reader can see what it costs. No pledged shares, no serial rights issues, no auditor change are disclosed — checked in [S2, S4, S9].

Related-party dealings are small in the trading line but not invisible on the balance sheet: US$3.3m of other receivables, of which US$3.2m is a loan to PT Filamendo Sakti, a subsidiary of Gajah Tunggal, on a ten-year term extended to 31 December 2027 at three per cent a year and denominated in rupiah [S4, F48, F50]. The same note shows US$0.8m of steam sales and rental income from Gajah Tunggal in the nine months, and names Provestment and Gajah Tunggal as the stockholders [S4, F49]. A three-per-cent loan to an affiliate when the group earns more than that on its deposits is a value transfer, but it is small against US$20.9m of cash and it is not the reason for the rating: a governance flag, not a manipulation-class flag. Ecogreen, which supplies three fifths of the raw materials, is not disclosed as a related party, so that contract is screened as a third-party purchase [S4]. No special-monitoring board status, no notation letters, no PSAK 16 revaluation — the land has been at cost since it was bought [S5, F31].

ESG: the Merak site is a chemicals plant on the Banten coast with the usual effluent and emissions exposure, and the ethoxylate chain carries palm-supply traceability risk through Ecogreen [S2, S4]. Neither is priced.

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 audit, the government's decision on the olefin and plastics safeguard, and the first-quarter 2027 statements [S2, S4, S10]. The KPIs we watch are the quarterly gross margin (does the Q3 loss repeat?), the ethoxylate run-rate against the nameplate capacity, the palm feedstock price against the deck CPO path, capex against depreciation, and any filing that puts terms on the land. A land sale or a plant shutdown would move the value more than anything in the P&L; a dividend resolution at the 2027 AGM would be the first sign the accumulated losses are being cleared.

bear.narrative: Dumped Chinese and Middle Eastern petrochemicals keep domestic utilisation at the bottom of the range and the ethoxylation spread goes through zero: the third-quarter 2026 gross loss of USD 0.745m becomes the run-rate and then worsens as the palm feedstock keeps rising, so the converter earns a negative spread and burns working capital and cash rather than throwing off the balance sheet. Volume holds, the ethylene glycol train keeps running at a fifth of capacity with no plan to fix it, and the equity is worth well under net cash because the cash is what funds the loss.

bull.narrative: A safeguard or anti-dumping package lifts the domestic reference price and the ethoxylate spread settles about a point and a half above our base, back near the second-quarter 2026 level, because the remedy removes the dumped barrel that sets the domestic price rather than because demand recovers; the glycol train is restarted on the higher reference price and revenue growth is eight points a year above base. No value is given in this scenario to a land sale or to realising the listed portfolio.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +31.8%: nine months of 2026 are already booked at USD 140.84m against USD 106.27m a year earlier (+32.5%) [S4, F9], and the fourth quarter is set at the third-quarter run-rate in both revenue and cost (Q3 alone was USD 49.84m of revenue after USD 91.01m at the half [S3, S4]), giving USD 190.7m for the year. The driver was feedstock pass-through plus capacity fill, not demand: raw materials used rose 35.1% to USD 113.79m over the same nine months [S4, F11] while the ethoxylate train is already at 90% of its 80,000 t capacity (71,941 t produced in FY2025) [S2, F6], so there is no volume headroom left for FY2027E. FY2027E +4.0% is the palm-linked feedstock (61% of COGS) carrying through at roughly the 2026 rate less the house Brent path: the deck runs Brent from 96.0 in FY2026E to 84.0 in FY2027E, and on the 5% of COGS that is Brent-linked and 90% passed through [S4] that shaves about half a point off dollar revenue, so the gross growth is a little above 4%. FY2028E-FY2030E +3.0% a year is Indonesian chemicals demand growth once the capacity fill is done, and the terminal rate 2.0% is below the explicit years, not above them.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The margin is the ethoxylation spread and it is thin. Nine months of 2026 printed 2.67% (gross profit USD 3.76m on USD 140.84m of sales) [S4, F10], against 1.13% for FY2025 and 0.94% for FY2024 [S5, F2, F4]. FY2026E is set so that the FULL YEAR reproduces the stated method - nine months booked plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate: Q3 alone was a gross LOSS of USD 0.745m (USD 3.760m at nine months less USD 4.505m at the half [S3, S4]), so the full year lands at an input of 1.78% at FY2026 input prices (the Brent link below adds about 0.2pp of cost). That 1.78% is then held flat in every forecast year and in perpetuity: it is the last actual year's economics reproduced, which is what the most-likely method requires. There is no CPO leak in the model and no step up: the 2026 tape shows the palm-derived feedstock from PT Ecogreen (61% of COGS [S4, F11, F12]) passing through, because revenue rose 32.5% with raw materials up 35.1% and the dollar gross profit still rose, and the loss-making polyester division is gone [S2, S6]. Equally there is no recovery: national petrochemical utilisation is 60%-70% on dumped imports and the association is asking for trade remedies, not reporting a demand recovery [S10, S7], so a spread above the last actual is not the most likely path. The Brent link moves the effective margin a few basis points around the 1.78% input because it is 5% of COGS at 90% pass-through.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Raw materials are 83% of cost of goods sold (USD 113.79m of USD 137.08m in the nine months to September 2026) and the largest single input by a wide margin is the palm-derived feedstock bought from PT Ecogreen Oleochemicals, USD 83.58m or 61% of COGS [S4, F11, F12]. That feedstock keys off the palm/CPO complex through biodiesel, not off crude one-for-one, so the Brent-linked share is the non-Ecogreen raw material at 22% of COGS [S4, F11, F12] further cut for the ethylene feed that only the glycol train consumes at a fifth of nameplate [S2, F21]: we apply 5% of COGS, not 20%, and the 2026 evidence supports a small number because raw materials rose 35.1% while revenue rose 32.5% and the gross margin still improved, so pass-through is close to complete [S4, F9, F11]. Net of the 90% pass-through that is 0.5% of COGS exposed, and the report states the modelled Brent effect from that figure.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Set at 90%. This is a converter with a 2%-3% gross margin: it quotes customers a formula price and the feedstock moves through within a quarter, which is why 2026 revenue rose 32.5% with raw materials up 35.1% and the spread barely moved [S4, F9, F11]. The 10% residual is the working-capital and timing leak. With link1_share at 5% the net exposure is half a per cent of COGS (5% x 10%), so the house Brent path from 96.0 in FY2026E to 84.0 in FY2027E moves gross profit by about 0.07% of COGS - around three per cent of the modelled gross profit, not enough on its own to swing the rating [S4].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Selling plus general and administrative expenses were USD 3.61m in the nine months to September 2026 (USD 0.16m selling, USD 3.45m G&A), 2.56% of revenue, and USD 4.97m for FY2025, 3.44% [S4, S5, F14]. The cost is essentially fixed in dollars (salaries USD 2.23m and employment benefits USD 0.45m of the G&A line [S4]), so we hold 2.6% on the higher 2026 revenue base rather than let the ratio drift as revenue moves.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: depreciation was USD 4.117m in FY2025 and USD 4.660m in FY2024, of which USD 3.879m ran through manufacturing cost and USD 0.011m through G&A in FY2025 [S5, F7, F8], against the data pack's USD 0.011m, which is only the G&A slice of the charge. Nine months of 2026 depreciation was USD 3.093m [S4], an annual rate of about 4.1m. Against the 2026 revenue base of USD 190.7m that is 2.2% and the charge is falling only slowly because capex (USD 0.41m in FY2025 [S5, F13]) is far below depreciation: the Merak plant is being sweated, not renewed.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capital expenditure was USD 0.41m, 0.3% of revenue, and nine months of 2026 USD 0.19m [S5, F13, S4]; the group sold USD 1.09m of property, plant and equipment in the same nine months, so it is shrinking its asset base, not building it [S4]. FY2026E is therefore the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate, like the revenue and cost lines: USD 0.19m + USD 0.06m = USD 0.25m, 0.13% of revenue, not the 0.4% that would imply a nine-fold Q4 step. The plant is being sweated, and the filing dates the end of that: S5 gives useful lives of five to twenty years for machinery and factory equipment and ten to twenty years for buildings [S5, p.33], and at 31 December 2025 net property, plant and equipment was USD 92.79m of which USD 65.08m is land carried at cost and never depreciated [S5, F36, F31], so the charge of USD 4.117m [S5, F7] runs against a depreciable remainder far smaller than the gross figure. On that arithmetic (net PP&E less land, over the annual charge) the average remaining life is in the high single digits, not the twenty-two years the total implies, and replacement of the two trains cannot be deferred much beyond the end of this decade. We therefore lift capex modestly to 0.2% and 0.3% of revenue in FY2027E-FY2028E, then ramp to 1.0% and 1.8% across FY2029E and FY2030E and settle at the D&A rate from FY2031E [S5], which is when that remaining life runs out and replacement can no longer be deferred; a perpetuity growing 2.0% a year cannot be funded by capex running below depreciation.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: At 30 September 2026 trade receivables of USD 16.41m plus inventories of USD 17.66m less trade payables of USD 32.84m gave net working capital of USD 1.23m, 0.87% of nine-month revenue [S4]: the supplier funds the business, with payables roughly double receivables. We set 1.0% of revenue, the September position, rather than the 1.9% the data pack shows for FY2025, because the payable balance is the structural feature and inventory has been run down from USD 24.37m at December to USD 17.66m [S4].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The group carries USD 154.2m of unappropriated accumulated losses at 30 September 2026 [S4, F17]. Nine months of 2026 paid USD 0.18m of tax on USD 4.63m of pre-tax profit, 3.9%, and FY2025 booked a net benefit [S4, S5]. That 3.9% is charged on pre-tax profit which at the operating line was close to zero, so the paid rate is already the after-shield rate and not a precursor to a ramp: the shield is 154.2m against pre-tax profit of the order of one million a year, and most of that pre-tax profit is interest income rather than the spread. The most-likely card requires the rate the LK shows being paid, so we hold 4%, the measured nine-month rate, through the forecast and in the terminal year, rather than ramp to the 22% statutory rate on an absorption schedule no filing supports.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The group has no bank debt: total liabilities of USD 43.12m at 30 September 2026 are trade payables, accruals, contract liabilities, taxes and an employment-benefit obligation, and the only borrowing-like item is USD 0.16m of lease liabilities [S4]. Finance costs of USD 0.04m in nine months are lease interest. Held at 8% on a negligible balance.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Finance income was USD 0.27m in the nine months to September 2026 on an opening cash balance of USD 10.04m and a closing one of USD 20.86m [S4], about 2.5% on the average; the balance is mostly rupiah and dollar deposits. We use 2.5% rather than the 1.7% historical ratio, which was depressed by a lower average balance.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No borrowing plan is disclosed and the group is net cash; the September 2026 balance sheet carries no bank debt [S4]. Zero in every year.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The reported profits are flattered by non-operating items that should not be forecast: nine months of 2026 booked a USD 1.29m fair-value gain on listed equity securities, USD 0.35m of foreign-exchange gains and USD 2.61m of other gains against an operating result of about USD 0.15m after SG&A [S4, F18]. They are excluded rather than repeated; the listed portfolio itself is carried in the engine's net debt through the separate balance-sheet line and the listed-securities fact [S4, F19], not through this line, so the gain is not double-counted.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: The only subsidiary carries negative net liabilities of USD 3,578 at 30 September 2026 and no profit for the period [S4]; held at zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid in the price history the pack carries (dps zero in FY2022A-FY2025A) [S0], and the annual general meeting of 2 June 2026 resolved not to distribute a dividend for FY2025 because the year was a loss [S9]. The balance sheet carries USD 154.2m of unappropriated accumulated losses [S4, F17], so there is no distributable reserve to pay a cash dividend from and the base pays nothing; the legal route to a distribution (a deficit reduction or capital reduction, then a dividend, or a buyback) is a governance event we discuss in the report rather than model, because no filing or resolution announces one [S9].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 3,889,179,559 shares issued and no corporate action in the pack or in the 2026 annual meeting resolutions [S0, S9]. The public holds 14.51% of the shares [S2, F29], above the exchange's free-float floor, so there is no dilution or index event in the base case; the thin float is handled as a liquidity discount on the target, not as a share-count change.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for a US dollar reporting currency, 2.0%, which is also the cap the constitution sets for a USD reporter. Indonesian petrochemical demand grows faster, but a single-site converter with a 2.4% gross margin, a 14.5% public float and a supplier that controls the cost base should not be given a growth premium in perpetuity.

challenges.challenge: The site bridge (USD 54.8m x 0.25 = USD 13.7m) is applied identically in base, bear and bull, so the scenario in which 'the site is worth more than its running value to a strategic buyer' still carries the site at 25%. Remove that unsourced 25% from the base and equity falls from 51.1m to 37.4m USD and the base value from Rp266 to ~Rp195: the 19.6% expected return is entirely the unsourced probability. At 100% the bull would be ~Rp680, not Rp467.
challenges.answer: Removed the site bridge item entirely: the unsourced 25% is gone, base and bull now carry no land sale, and the base falls to the engine value. §4 shows the 853,205 m2 at USD 65.08m cost so the option can be sized, and says the bull is a floor for a sale case, not a ceiling. Post-BS note records that no filing states a buyer, price or timetable [S5, F31].

challenges.challenge: The 20% liquidity discount is applied to the whole target although ~74% of the value (USD 29.6m net cash plus the portfolio) is realisable cash and quoted securities. A 20% haircut on cash removes ~Rp40-45 per share with no source, and no bull case gives any value to a capital return even though the USD 154.2m loss shield would make one tax-free.
challenges.answer: Kept the discount because it is the engine's house rule, applied to the whole target at 20% for measured ADTV of Rp0.23bn, and disclosed it as such in §6. §4 now prints the pre-discount values (weighted target and base) beside the post-discount target so the cost to the cash-backed components is visible [S4, S0].

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative says 'the listed portfolio is realised with the proceeds available to minorities', but no scenario carries a realisation value: USD 8.87m is marked at 80% in every case. No bull either for the USD 3.16m non-current loan to PT Filamendo Sakti and the USD 3.33m of related-party receivables being repaid.
challenges.answer: Deleted the portfolio-realism clause from the bull narrative: the listed securities stay inside cash at market value less the 20% haircut in every scenario, and no scenario claims proceeds available to minorities. The related-party loan is now reported in §6 [S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says a margin deterioration 'takes the operating value to zero, at which point the equity is worth the net cash', but the model's own grid returns 0.0 at -2pp margin with +2pp growth: below roughly break-even the converter burns the cash, so the downside is not floored at Rp150. The report's bear stops at -1.3pp margin and never shows the case that removes the net cash.
challenges.answer: Corrected the claim: §4 and §5 now say the downside is not floored at net cash because below break-even the converter burns the cash, and the bear was widened to a through-zero spread so the case that consumes the balance sheet is the one shown [S4, S3].

challenges.challenge: The bull's main driver is the INAPLAS safeguard/BMAD request [S10], but INAPLAS is the olefin, aromatics and plastics association; ethoxylate/EOD output (71,941 t, the better-margin product) is not in that remit. Section 2 nevertheless says a duty 'on the products it makes' would raise the reference price across the slate.
challenges.answer: Narrowed the remedy claim: §2 now states that INAPLAS covers olefins, aromatics and plastics and that ethoxylate/EOD is outside its remit, so a duty reaches the glycol/MEG chain only, which management says is loss-making, not the better-margin slate [S10, S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2027E carries an effective gross margin of 2.49% (input 2.6%) while FY2026E is 1.58% and the latest quarter was a gross loss of USD 0.745m (-1.5%). The +0.9pp step in the first full forecast year rests only on the 9M average that the losing Q3 already dilutes, and the two years use incompatible methods. The step is worth roughly Rp30 of the base.
challenges.answer: FY2027E now holds the FY2026E actual margin instead of stepping up to a 2.6% input: the Q3 2026 gross loss is the latest and most complete read, and the nine-month average that sourced the old step is diluted by the same quarter [S4, S3].

challenges.challenge: Palm feedstock is 61% of COGS and has no cost link in the model, so holding the gross margin percentage fixed assumes 100% pass-through of the deck's rising CPO path (1,007 to 1,135 in FY2026E, +12.7%), while link1_pass states only 90% pass-through. A 10% leak on that input is ~USD 1.5m a year, more than the entire FY2027E net profit of USD 0.36m.
challenges.answer: The palm link is passed through in full on the 2026 evidence: revenue and raw materials both rose about a third with dollar gross profit rising, so a 10% leak would have taken the spread to zero and did not. The 90% is Brent at 5% of COGS, not palm; the bear carries the palm leak [S4, F9, F11, F10].

challenges.challenge: S11 is the company's financial-statements download page. It supports 'Q3 2026 is the latest filing' but cannot support the post_bs_review claim that there was 'no presentation, public expose or corporate action' after the accounts; the signing date of 29 October 2026 is in S4 (p.3, p.67), not S11. S6 is also cited for the Q3 gross loss and the deck Brent/CPO paths and the WACC build are cited to S4.
challenges.answer: post_bs_review rewritten: S4 p.3 and p.67 carry the 29 October 2026 signing date, S11 is cited only for the latest filing on the company site, and the claim of no corporate action is limited to the registered press sources searched to 12 November 2026, not the IDX feed [S4, S11, S2, S9].

challenges.challenge: The FCFE yield renders as 0.1% because the model stores 0.0921 and the pctv formatter expects a percent number, so a 9.2% FCFE yield prints as 0.1%. The next sentence says 'the yield is high', contradicting the figure it is used to support, and this is the cross-check the report says it takes most seriously.
challenges.answer: Dropped the pctv formatter on the FCFE yield so it prints the model's 6.3% rather than 0.1%, and re-stated the argument against the correct number: the yield is retained cash from a no-dividend, no-capex year, not a distribution to minorities [S4, S9].

challenges.challenge: The DCF uses Sept net cash of USD 29.6m but the cross-checks use the model's forecast net-debt line: FY2027E -23.9m gives EV/EBITDA 4.1x where the DCF's own net cash gives ~1.9x. FY2026E net debt of -20.2m also implies December cash falls from 29.7m in September to 20.2m while FCFF is +2.4m, so the forecast balance sheet does not start from the latest_bs the report says it rolled to.
challenges.answer: §4 now states that the multiples table uses the model's forecast net-debt line rolled from the FY2025A audited balance sheet while the DCF uses the 30 September net cash, that the two are not on the same basis, and that on the DCF basis FY2027E EV/EBITDA is roughly half the printed figure [S4].

challenges.challenge: The land bridge is a stale net: 54.8 = 65.08 land at cost less the PREVIOUS operating EV of 10.23 (round-1 C5 response), whereas the current EV is 9.62, so the item should be 55.46. The label says 'Merak and Karawang land' but the amount is all three parcels (USD 65.08m, F31); the -1.77m (20%) portfolio haircut is applied but its size is never stated in the report.
challenges.answer: Moot after the removal: the stale net, the Merak/Karawang label and the portfolio hedge are gone with the item. The remaining bridge item is the portfolio haircut, now labelled as 20% of the USD 8.87m listed securities and stated in §4 [S4, F19].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E capex of USD 0.76m (0.4% of revenue) against 9M actual capex of USD 0.19m implies Q4 capex of 0.57m, a 9x step on the quarterly run-rate, in the same update that says the forecast is unchanged and that the group sold 1.09m of PP&E in the nine months.
challenges.answer: FY2026E capex set at the 9M actual plus Q4 at the Q3 run-rate, 0.13% of revenue, instead of a nine-fold Q4 step; FY2027E-FY2028E lift only to 0.2% and 0.3% before the late-life reset [S5, S4].

challenges.challenge: The +-0.04 growth shock is applied to a.revenue_growth for every forecast year including FY2026E, so the bear's FY2026E revenue is 184.9m and the bull's 196.5m, against the 190.7m that nine months booked plus Q4 at the Q3 rate imply. The scenarios therefore contradict the anchor the base case rests on.
challenges.answer: §5 now states that the growth shock is applied to every forecast year including the banked FY2026E, that the base anchor is unchanged, and that the scenarios are a sensitivity on the whole path rather than a re-forecast of FY2026E [S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says related-party dealings are small in the trading line and larger only on the balance-sheet portfolio, but S4 note 8 shows USD 3.33m of related-party receivables including a USD 3.16m non-current loan to PT Filamendo Sakti at 3% maturing 31 December 2027, plus a USD 0.13m payable; the loan is not mentioned anywhere.
challenges.answer: §6 now reports the related-party receivables including the non-current loan to PT Filamendo Sakti at 3% maturing December 2027 and the small payable, and says a 3% loan against deposit rates is a governance flag, not a manipulation-class flag [S4].

challenges.challenge: The report is 7,889 words against the 500-3,500 range for a results update, with section 3 alone at 1,768 words. The length is mostly restatement of the initiation rather than the Q3 roll the update is supposed to cover.
challenges.answer: Cut the report to 2,390 words, inside the results-update range, keeping the Q3 evidence, the valuation change and the scenario rewrite and dropping the initiation restatement [S4, S3].

missing_bull_case.note: The site is the thesis yet the bull case hands it the same 25% weight as base: at 100% the bull is ~Rp680, not Rp467. No bull for deploying the USD 29.6m net cash, for a deficit reduction that unlocks a dividend, or for the USD 3.16m related-party loan being repaid.

missing_bear_case.note: Net cash is not a floor: the model's own margin/growth grid returns 0.0 at -2pp margin and +2pp growth, contradicting the claim that equity is then worth the net cash. No bear for the INAPLAS remedy covering olefin/aromatics/plastics and not ethoxylates, nor for HGB rights expiring from 2027 on part of the 853,205 m2.

assumption_realism.note: FY2027E effective gross margin 2.49% against a Q3 2026 gross loss of -1.5% and FY2026E at 1.58%: a +0.9pp step one year after the losing quarter, sourced only to the 9M average. The model also assumes 100% pass-through on the palm feedstock (61% of COGS) while stating 90% on all inputs.

evidence_and_citations.note: S4 and S11 correctly support the signing date (S4 p.3, p.67) and Q3 as the latest filing; every figure in the prose is tokenised (no typed currency, checked). Failures: S11 (a financial-statements list) is cited for 'no corporate action', S6 for the Q3 gross loss, and the deck Brent/CPO paths plus the WACC build to S4.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-only weights are justified on a name where EBITDA is depreciation. But the bridge is applied inside every scenario at 25%, so the largest lever never reaches full value in the bull; the net-debt line in the cross-checks (-23.9 FY2027E) is not the Sept net cash (-29.6) the DCF uses; and the land item is a stale net of the prior EV.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose says the rating rests on the site while the target carries only a quarter of it. The FCFE yield renders 0.1% where the model holds 0.0921, and the next sentence calls it high. The report also still narrates the reverse DCF (25.4%) that round-1 C14 was accepted as removed.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck paths resolve correctly and Brent spot/FY2027E match the brief (92.1/84.0), with Brent wired at 5% of COGS x 10% leak. But the CPO path the report calls the real cost driver is not wired to margin at all: a fixed margin assumes 100% pass-through on the 61% palm input, which is not what link1_pass states.

conservatism_audit.note: The 25% site probability (Rp71 of the Rp266 base) is unsourced and it is the whole return. The site is all three land parcels but the label says Merak and Karawang; 54.8 nets out the prior EV 10.23 not the current 9.62; the -1.77 portfolio haircut is applied but never stated; FY2026E capex implies a 9x Q4 step.

calibration.note: qc passes with no BLOCK and the model reproduces FY2025A exactly from the restated facts (EBIT -3.34, D&A 4.12, EBITDA 0.78). The ebitda_margin gap of 0.65pp is 120% of the 0.54% actual, but the gate is near-degenerate because EBITDA is 96% depreciation.

signoff.notes: SELL Rp108 against Rp192 is supported on the desk's own method. The operating business does not earn its depreciation (9M2026 gross profit US$3.76m on US$140.84m of sales, Q3 a gross loss of US$0.745m), so the operating EV is negative in the model and the equity value is the September net liquid assets rolled forward and discounted once at the target. Holding the spread at the last actual instead of stepping it up is the MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE rule, not a haircut, and the removal of the unsourced 25% land probability was the red team's own C15 requirement, so the move from the 7 November ADD is a correction of an unsourced input rather than a discretionary downgrade. The land option is disclosed at its US$65.1m carrying value and is not valued at zero silently. Scenario shocks are mirrored (growth plus/minus 4pp, margin plus/minus 1.7pp) and the batch-wide Brent deck is applied as a cost line, not as a margin uplift. Two residual QC FIX items are noted for the next cycle and are not rating-moving: the summary still says the previous model "jumped to a 1.8% input" where Q12 established 2.6% (the ~Rp100 bridge slice is right in quantum on 2.6% to 1.78%, roughly Rp84-94), and Q13's US$1.6m in section 3 should read US$1.3m for the 9M2025 comparative. Neither changes the target, the bridge direction or the rating. One point to carry: the target sits below the Rp139 a share of net cash plus quoted securities, so the SELL is a statement that the market pays 1.4x liquid assets for a loss-making converter, not that the cash is impaired.

bias.note: Round-2 audit: base FY2027E gross margin 1.665% sits 0.53pp above FY2025A actual (1.13%) but only 0.09pp above the FY2026E build, so no step-up haircut remains; the calibration gap is 0.65pp of EBITDA margin with the model ABOVE the last actual, i.e. mildly optimistic, not bearish [S5, F2, F4, S4]. The bearish side is the perpetuity: DCF EV -9.7m against a site carried at 65.1m [S5, F31], so the base prices the land below zero by assuming the converter runs forever - disclosed in sections 4 and 5, and the engine clips the bear at 0 rather than its -Rp20 unclipped value, which cuts the other way. Scenarios mirrored (+-0.017 margin, +-0.04 growth), base 50%. Net direction neutral.

findings.finding: Investment summary says the previous model jumped to a 1.8% input for FY2027E. The prior input was 2.6% (effective 2.49%): the accepted C20 answer and section 3 say two-and-a-half per cent, and 1.78% is the CURRENT flat input. The ~Rp100 a share attributed to this change reconciles only on 2.6% -> 1.665% (0.93pp x 198.3m = 1.85m gross profit, ~11x = ~Rp94), not on a 0.14pp change (~Rp14).

Section 3 Costs says dollar gross profit rose from US$1.6m to a nine-month US$3.8m. The 9M2025 comparative is US$1.344m (F43, S4); US$1.6m is the FY2025A full-year figure (F1-F2). The same section states it correctly two paragraphs earlier as US$1.3m.
Section 3 pairs EBIT of US$-1.8m with depreciation of US$4.3m. FY2026E EBIT is -1.852 on DA 4.118; 4.283 is the FY2027E charge, so the sentence mixes years [model lines].

The -9.7m EV in the base implies the 853,205 m2 site carried at US$65.08m is worth less than nothing, because the perpetuity assumes the converter never shuts. Disclosed in sections 4 and 5, but the reader is only told a sale would add a multiple of the gap [S5, F31].
The weights.changed justification says the government describes the industry as oversupplied [S10]; S10 is INAPLAS, the industry association, protesting to Kemenperin, not the government.

flags.message: expected return -44%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is the sum of three deliberate, sourced cuts, not a drift: (i) the unsourced 25% land-sale probability is removed because no filing states a buyer, a price or a timetable for the 853,205 m2 carried at USD 65.08m [S5, F31]; (ii) FY2027E gross margin is held at the FY2026E actual rather than stepped up, because the latest quarter printed a gross loss [S4, S3]; (iii) the operating EV is negative because EBIT does not cover depreciation and capex must reset to the D&A rate once the remaining life runs out: S5's useful lives are five to twenty years for machinery and ten to twenty for buildings, and most of the USD 92.79m net PP&E is the USD 65.08m of non-depreciable land, so the depreciable remainder is short [S5, p.33, F36, F31]. What the price implies: Rp192 is about 1.4x the 30 September net liquid assets per share, so the market is paying for the land option and a spread recovery that no filing supports; the reverse DCF cannot bracket the price on any revenue growth, which is itself the point [S4].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The valuation weights use only DCF (dcf_fcff 1.0). Multiples are unusable for a business whose operating profit is about USD 0.2m: nine-month 2026 net profit of USD 4.45m rests on USD 4.25m of fair-value, FX and other gains below the operating line [S4, F18], so a price-earnings multiple would value non-operating items, and LTM EBITDA after restated depreciation is almost entirely the depreciation charge, making EV/EBITDA a multiple of an accounting entry. A price-to-book cross-check at book equity of USD 117.1m [S4] would value the company at several times the market price, because the book is a glycol plant running at a fifth of nameplate in an industry the government describes as oversupplied [S10]; we give it zero weight. The DCF alone captures the going-concern cash flow.
